name: MCP2515
full_name: Stand-alone CAN controller with SPI interface
description: Stand-alone CAN 2.0B controller that adds a complete CAN protocol engine to any micro over SPI (up to 10 MHz). It handles message framing, filtering (two acceptance masks, six filters), and error management, with three transmit and two receive buffers. It is only the controller: it needs an external CAN transceiver (e.g. MCP2551/TJA1050) on the bus side and an external crystal/oscillator (8/16/20 MHz). The workhorse behind nearly every hobbyist CAN shield.

pins.name: TXCAN
pins.description: transmit output to the CAN transceiver TXD

pins.name: RXCAN
pins.description: receive input from the CAN transceiver RXD

pins.name: CLKOUT/SOF
pins.description: clock output (prescaled) or start-of-frame signal, configurable

pins.name: TX0RTS
pins.description: request-to-send for TX buffer 0 (or general-purpose input)

pins.name: TX1RTS
pins.description: request-to-send for TX buffer 1 (or general-purpose input)

pins.name: TX2RTS
pins.description: request-to-send for TX buffer 2 (or general-purpose input)

pins.name: OSC1
pins.description: crystal/resonator oscillator input (or external clock in)

pins.name: RX1BF
pins.description: receive buffer 1 full / interrupt or general-purpose output

pins.name: RX0BF
pins.description: receive buffer 0 full / interrupt or general-purpose output

pins.name: INT
pins.description: active-low interrupt to the host MCU

extra.spi: up to 10 MHz, SPI modes (0,0) and (1,1)

typical_application: Add a CAN 2.0B port to any SPI-capable microcontroller: MCP2515 controller + MCP2551/TJA1050 transceiver + crystal, the standard hobbyist CAN-shield recipe.
gotchas: it is a controller ONLY - it has no bus driver; you must add an external CAN transceiver (MCP2551, TJA1050, SN65HVD230) between RXCAN/TXCAN and the bus
needs an external crystal or oscillator (8/16/20 MHz); the chosen frequency sets the achievable CAN bit timing - get it wrong and the bit rate is off
SPI mode must be (0,0) or (1,1); other modes will not communicate
VDD is 2.7-5.5 V, but a 5 V MCP2551 transceiver needs 5 V - mind level differences when running the controller at 3.3 V
the bus still needs 120 ohm termination at both physical ends; the chip does not provide it
